The thin lines draw a pentagram structure, in which F and G are on EB, F is the intersection of AD and EB, G is the intersection of AC and EB; J and H are interior intersections, H is at the intersection of AC and BD, J and H are symmetrically located on the left and right sides, and JH is an interior horizontal line. The problem gives AG=1. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, place the regular pentagon on the unit circle, taking A=(0,1), B=(cos18°,sin18°), C=(cos54°,-sin54°), D=(-cos54°,-sin54°), E=(-cos18°,sin18°). Let φ=(1+√5)/2. It is known that sin18°=1/(2φ), sin54°=φ/2, and for a regular pentagon, the long diagonal AC=φ·CD. G is on AC, set G=A+t(C-A). Because G is also on the horizontal line EB, its y-coordinate is sin18°: 1-t(1+sin54°)=sin18°. Substituting sin18°=1/(2φ), sin54°=φ/2, get t=1/φ². Therefore AG=t·AC=AC/φ². F and G are symmetric about the vertical axis, and correspond to the same parameter t=1/φ², so FG=t·CD. Also AC=φ·CD, therefore FG=t·CD=(AC/φ²)/φ=AG/φ. H is the intersection of AC and BD. Set H=A+t(C-A), and at the same time H=B+u(D-B). Solving the coordinate equations of the two lines gives t=1/φ. The symmetric point J is on AD at the same height, so JH=t·CD=CD/φ. Since AG=AC/φ²=(φ·CD)/φ²=CD/φ, JH=AG. Also CD=φ·AG. The problem gives AG=1, therefore FG=1/φ, JH=1, CD=φ. Thus FG+JH+CD=1/φ+1+φ=1+(φ+1/φ)=1+√5.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/analytic route. From the image, read that the thick outer polygon is the regular pentagon ABCDE with A at the top, EB and CD horizontal, and the thin drawn diagonals form a pentagram: F=AD∩EB, G=AC∩EB, J=AD∩CE, H=AC∩BD. Put a regular pentagon on the unit circle, e.g. A=(0,1), B=(cos18°,sin18°), C=(cos54°,-sin54°), D=(-cos54°,-sin54°), E=(-cos18°,sin18°). Compute G as AC∩EB and F symmetrically as AD∩EB; compute H=AC∩BD and J symmetrically. This gives, in the unit-circle scale, AG=d/φ^2, FG=AG/φ, JH=AG, and CD=φ·AG, where φ=(1+√5)/2. Then use the text fact AG=1, so FG=1/φ, JH=1, CD=φ, and FG+JH+CD=1+φ+1/φ=1+√5.

method.method_draft: Synthetic pentagram/golden-ratio route. From the image, treat the thin segments as the five diagonals of the regular pentagon, whose intersections form the smaller regular pentagon FGH IJ. By symmetry, AF=AG, and the angle between diagonals AD and AC at A is 36°, so triangle AFG is a golden isosceles triangle with equal sides AG=AF=1; hence FG=2sin18°=1/φ. The central polygon FGH IJ is regular, so JH is a diagonal of the small pentagon with side FG, giving JH=φ·FG=1. 推理：按正五边形和五角星的对称性，F 与 G 关于竖直对称轴对称，所以 AF=AG=1。角 FAG 是正五边形中从 A 发出的两条对角线 AD 与 AC 的夹角，等于 36°。因此三角形 AFG 是顶角 36°、腰长 1 的等腰三角形，所以 FG=2sin18°。利用黄金比 φ=(1+√5)/2，有 2sin18°=1/φ，因此 FG=1/φ。内部小五边形 FGH IJ 是正五边形，JH 是该小正五边形的一条对角线，而正五边形的对角线等于边长的 φ 倍，所以 JH=φ·FG=1。外部正五边形边长 CD 与内部小正五边形边长 FG 的比例为 φ²:1，所以 CD=φ²·FG=φ。于是 FG+JH+CD=1/φ+1+φ。又 φ+1/φ=√5，所以结果为 1+√5。

Image description: The thick-line outer frame in the figure is regular pentagon ABCDE, A is at the top, B is at the upper right, C is at the lower right, D is at the lower left, E is at the upper left; EB is the upper horizontal line, and CD is the lower horizontal side. The thin lines draw a pentagram structure, in which F and G are on EB, F is the intersection of AD and EB, G is the intersection of AC and EB; J and H are interior intersections, H is at the intersection of AC and BD, J and H are symmetrically located on the left and right sides, and JH is an interior horizontal line. The problem gives AG=1.

Reasoning: By the coordinate method, place the regular pentagon on the unit circle, taking A=(0,1), B=(cos18°,sin18°), C=(cos54°,-sin54°), D=(-cos54°,-sin54°), E=(-cos18°,sin18°). Let φ=(1+√5)/2. It is known that sin18°=1/(2φ), sin54°=φ/2, and for a regular pentagon, the long diagonal AC=φ·CD.

G is on AC, set G=A+t(C-A). Because G is also on the horizontal line EB, its y-coordinate is sin18°: 1-t(1+sin54°)=sin18°. Substituting sin18°=1/(2φ), sin54°=φ/2, get t=1/φ². Therefore AG=t·AC=AC/φ².

F and G are symmetric about the vertical axis, and correspond to the same parameter t=1/φ², so FG=t·CD. Also AC=φ·CD, therefore FG=t·CD=(AC/φ²)/φ=AG/φ.

H is the intersection of AC and BD. Set H=A+t(C-A), and at the same time H=B+u(D-B). Solving the coordinate equations of the two lines gives t=1/φ. The symmetric point J is on AD at the same height, so JH=t·CD=CD/φ. Since AG=AC/φ²=(φ·CD)/φ²=CD/φ, JH=AG.

Also CD=φ·AG. The problem gives AG=1, therefore FG=1/φ, JH=1, CD=φ. Thus FG+JH+CD=1/φ+1+φ=1+(φ+1/φ)=1+√5.
